column15: Independent bottler - single cask/small batch/limited-edition bottlings; official site states it is a trading name of Atom Supplies Limited (England and Wales). No house peat level. Sample product names (FEW, Puni, TBWC, Helsinki, Mackmyra, Paul John) span distilleries worldwide; distillery rows emitted for few/puni/helsinki-distilling/mackmyra/paul-john per rule 2.

Craft distillery, likely Evanston, Illinois (847 area code on official site; not explicitly stated there). Makes bourbon/rye/other grain whiskeys; no peated product found. peatProfile rests on the general category fact that peat is rarely used outside Scotland, not a distillery-specific statement.

Italian single malt distillery, Glurns, Venosta Valley, South Tyrol. Official site's current range (Core/ARTE/AURA/CUBO) shows no peated expression; combined with the general category fact that peat is rare outside Scotland.

Helsinki, Finland; founded 2014, described as the first distillery in Helsinki in over a century. Named in TBWC's sample products. Could not confirm peat status within budget - left unknown rather than guessed.

Swedish single malt distillery. Wikipedia confirms Mackmyra sources peat from a local bog near Osterfarnebo for use in some whisky, but this is not stated as a uniform house style across the whole range, so left unknown rather than none/light. Filed for bankruptcy August 2024; post-bankruptcy ownership not confirmed this session.

Made in Goa, India. Core range (Brilliance, Edited, Nirvana, Classic/Oloroso/PX Select Cask) is unpeated 6-row Indian barley. A distinct 'Peated Select Cask' line uses imported Islay and Aberdeen peat - see rule.tsv (pattern Peated -> heavy).

Region/owner from the local Scottish-distilleries authority file. Peat claim rests on the Highland region's general character per the Scotch whisky Wikipedia Region section ('fruity, sweet, spicy, malty', no smoke mentioned there), not a Dalmore-specific statement - kept low confidence despite being well known in whisky literature as unpeated.
Same basis as Dalmore - Highland regional-character citation, not distillery-specific.

Dublin (Blackpitts area) distillery, owned by Bacardi. Core range is unpeated; Blackpitts is an explicit exception, officially branded 'Blackpitts Peated Single Malt' on teelingwhiskey.com - see rule.tsv. defaultTypeName left empty because the range spans single malt, single grain and small-batch blends.

Input brand string '& Whisky' does not correspond to any single identifiable producer - its 6 sample product names (Umiki, Kura The, Lord Moisans, Scottish Piper, MacKinlay's Old) look like several unrelated real brands (Japanese blends, MacKinlay's Scotch) rather than one house style. Likely a catalogue category/parsing artifact, not a real brand. Not researched as a single entity; alias emitted only for the exact catalogue string as required.

Budget blended Scotch label (incl. a 'Bourbon Finish' variant per sample); owner not confirmed this session. peatProfile rests on the general Highland/Speyside/Lowland-dominated blend character described on the Scotch whisky Wikipedia page (only Islay/Campbeltown are described there as peaty/smoky), not brand-specific evidence.

All 6 samples are just 'Glendale' with no distinguishing detail. No distillery of this name appears in the Scottish-distilleries authority file, so treated as a generic Scotch-sounding own-label blend rather than a real distillery; peatProfile via the same general regional-character inference as Black Ram.

Blended malt whisky (originally Balvenie+Glenfiddich+Kininvie; current recipe undisclosed but Wikipedia states constituent malts remain Speyside-sourced) - unpeated core range. 'Smokey Monkey' is a distinct limited-batch blend Wikipedia states includes Islay whiskies - see rule.tsv (pattern Smokey -> medium, since Islay malt is only one part of that blend).

'Deveron'/'The Deveron'/'Glen Deveron' is the retail single-malt brand name of Macduff distillery's own malt (Wikipedia: Macduff 'produces single malt whisky called The Deveron as 10, 12 and 18 year old expressions'). peatProfile via Highland regional-character citation, not brand-specific - Macduff malt is also a major component of William Lawson blends per Wikipedia, where undisclosed detail could differ.

Founded 1960; owned by John Dewar & Sons under Bacardi since 1992 (per Wikipedia). Malt sold under the 'Deveron'/'Glen Deveron' brand (see deveron row) and used in William Lawson blends. Added because 'deveron' (from my input list) needs this distillery as its parentSlug. peatProfile via Highland regional citation, not distillery-specific.

First French single malt (launched 1998), made by the Warenghem Distillery in Brittany. No peat information confirmed either way this session. FOR REVIEWER: the 'Yeun Elez' expression (in my sample list) is named for a peat bog/moor in the Monts d'Arree, Brittany, by Breton place-name - it may well be a peated bottling distinct from the 'Classic' line, but I found no fetched source confirming this; worth checking before assuming the whole range is uniform.

English whisky distillery, Bassenthwaite Lake, Cumbria; bought by winemaker Nyetimber in 2024 (previously independent, founded 2014 by Paul Currie). Sample names (Equinox, Galaxia, Resfeber, Nostalgia, Signature, Whiskymaker's Reserve No.7) are all distinct experimental releases with no stated common peat level - genuinely appears to vary by release, so left unknown rather than guessed.
No information found. 'Honey' and 'Spisy' [sic, likely 'Spicy'] variants suggest a flavored whisky-based product; origin and type could not be determined within budget.

Region/owner from the Scottish-distilleries authority file. Peat claim via the Speyside region's general character (Wikipedia's Speyside single malt page: 'the use of peat is not common here, so many of the whiskies are not smoky'), not distillery-specific.

Suntory's flagship single malt distillery (Osaka). The Wikipedia article makes no mention of peat or smoke anywhere in its text, consistent with Yamazaki's well-known fruity/sherry-driven house style (contrast sister distillery Hakushu, which has an explicit peated limited line). No sentence directly states 'unpeated', so kept at low confidence.
Same Speyside regional-character basis as Glen Keith.

Independent craft distillery, Galway, founded 2016 (per Wikipedia's List of whiskey distilleries in Ireland). 'SPS' in two sample names likely means 'Single Pot Still' but the range also includes other styles (Small Batch, Long Walk), so defaultTypeName left empty. peatProfile via the general Irish-whiskey category fact (peat rarely used outside Scotland), not distillery-specific.

FLAG FOR REVIEW (positive peat claim). Official site describes Highland peat smoke across the whole range, from 'very subtle hints' (Legacy) to 'classic peat'/'full and rich...Highland peat smoke flavours' (Tradition) to 'traditional Highland peat smoke notes' (Triple Wood) - consistently present but explicitly softer than Islay heavyweights, so classified medium rather than heavy. Historically the peat component of Teacher's Highland Cream blend.

Independent craft distillery, County Cork, founded 2016. One sample ('Double Oak Blend') indicates the range includes a blend, so defaultTypeName left empty. peatProfile via general Irish-whiskey category fact, not distillery-specific.

Region/owner from the authority file. Peat claim via the Lowland region's general character on the Scotch whisky Wikipedia page ('soft and smooth...floral nose...lighter, sweet and floral tones', no smoke), not distillery-specific. Lowland malts are the most reliably unpeated Scotch category.

Blended Scotch whisky brand; no dedicated Wikipedia article found. FOR REVIEWER: I recall from general knowledge, NOT verified via a fetched source this session, that Lauder's is produced by MacDuff International Ltd - left owner blank rather than asserting it. peatProfile via the same general blend-character inference as Black Ram/Glendale.
Same Highland regional-character basis as Dalmore/Glencadam/Macduff.

Vermont rye whiskey producer, Shoreham. peatProfile via the general 'peat rarely used outside Scotland' category fact plus the well-established production fact that American rye/bourbon malting does not use peat smoke; not a WhistlePig-specific statement. Catalogue spells the brand 'Whistlepig' (lowercase p); official spelling is 'WhistlePig'.

Believed to be Boone County Distilling Co. (Independence, Kentucky) from general knowledge - not verified via a fetched source this session, so the kind=distillery call is a judgment call, not a confirmed fact. peatProfile via the generic bourbon-category fact (charred-oak/corn-mash process, no peat-smoking step described anywhere for bourbon production), not brand-specific.

Irish whiskey brand; could not confirm producer/distillery this session (a Wikipedia search only turned up an unrelated folk band of the same name). One sample is 'De Danann Walsh', suggesting a possible link to an Irish producer named Walsh - not confirmed. peatProfile via general Irish-whiskey category fact.

FLAG FOR REVIEW (positive peat claim, indirectly supported). Wikipedia's Hakushu distillery page lists a 2013 'Heavily Peated' release as a distinct LIMITED series, separate from the core range (which includes the 12 Year Old and the 'Distiller's Reserve' in my samples), implying the standard range is not heavily peated. I did not find an explicit statement of the core range's own smoke level in a fetched source - 'light' reflects general knowledge that standard Hakushu carries a subtle/herbal smokiness, not a directly quoted fact. Treat with caution; a stronger citation would help confirm.

No dedicated source found for this exact brand name (search only surfaced unrelated one-off 'Coronation of King Charles III' commemorative editions from other brands). Treated as a generic royalty-themed own-label blended Scotch; peatProfile via general blend-character inference, not brand-specific.
No information found for this brand within budget (Wikipedia search returned only unrelated people/topics named Oakeshott). Origin and type unknown.

'The Sexton Irish Whiskey' confirmed as a product of Proximo Spirits (Wikipedia disambiguation page). Marketed as single malt Irish whiskey from an undisclosed source distillery; kind=blend used only as the closest available bucket for an undisclosed-origin label per rule 3 in the brief, not because it is actually a blended-type whiskey. peatProfile via general Irish-whiskey category fact.

Owner per the authority file (Elixir Distillers acquired Tormore from Chivas Brothers/Pernod Ricard in 2024, consistent with general knowledge). peatProfile via Speyside regional-character citation, not distillery-specific.
No information found for this brand within budget (no Wikipedia coverage). Single sample 'Aikan Extra Collection Batch No.3' gives no clear indication of origin, distillery or type.

Wikipedia: the modern 'Bomberger's'-branded whiskey (e.g. 'Bomberger's Declaration' in my sample) is a Michter's product with 'no direct connection' to the historic 1753-1989 Bomberger's/Michter's Distillery site in Pennsylvania (a National Historic Landmark, now non-operating). parentSlug=michters is not a row in my own producer.tsv - Michter's is a well-known US whiskey brand/producer another batch will very likely cover; flag if it does not. peatProfile via the generic bourbon-category fact.
No information found within budget. Single sample name is 'Gold Mill', which does not obviously relate to the brand name 'Dilmoor' - origin and type could not be determined.

No distillery of this name appears in the Scottish-distilleries authority file. Generic Scotch-sounding own-label name, likely a discount-retail blended Scotch (cf. Aldi's 'Glen Marnoch') - not verified via a fetched source this session. peatProfile via general blend-character inference.
No information found within budget. Single sample 'Hogs 3' gives no clear indication of style, origin or the meaning of '3'.

Confirmed premium single malt Irish whiskey brand, produced by Irish Distillers (Pernod Ricard), introduced 1998, named for Knappogue Castle in County Clare. Source distillery undisclosed for current releases; kind=blend used as the closest available bucket for an undisclosed-origin single-malt label (rule 3 in the brief), not because it is blended-type whiskey. peatProfile via general Irish-whiskey category fact.

Confirmed via Wikipedia: 'a range of single malt Scotch whiskies from four of Scotland's key whisky distilling regions - Highland, Islay, Speyside and Lowland', supplied by parent company Morrison Bowmore Distillers; 'there is no McClelland's distillery per se'. Because the range explicitly includes an Islay (typically peated) variant and my input sample carries no region qualifier, peatProfile is deliberately left unknown rather than guessed - this one product could be any of the four regions.
No information found within budget (no Wikipedia coverage). Origin and type undetermined.
Confirmed blend of Highland and Lowland malts, historically made at Seagram's Speyside distilleries, now owned by Chivas Brothers/Pernod Ricard; introduced 1965. No Islay/peated component described.

Catalogue spells the brand 'Roe + Co'; official/Wikipedia spelling is 'Roe & Co'. Distillery established 2019 in Dublin (Thomas Street), owned by Diageo; flagship product is a Blended Irish whiskey. No peat/smoke mentioned.

Confirmed as a real distillery via its inclusion in Wikipedia's American Whiskey Trail list (West Virginia craft distillery per general knowledge, not itself stated on that page). Makes bourbon, rye and a 'Contradiction' wheated bourbon (per my sample); defaultTypeName left empty since the range spans types. peatProfile via the generic bourbon/rye-category fact.

No source found for this specific brand. 'Highland Shepherd' reads as a generic pastoral-themed Scotch own-label name; treated as a supermarket-style blend by convention, not confirmed. peatProfile via general blend-character inference - genuinely marginal, could reasonably also be left unknown.

Danville, Kentucky; founded 2013 by Dr. Pat Heist and Shane Baker (Wikipedia). Makes wheated bourbon, rye-forward bourbon and rye whiskey - defaultTypeName left empty since the range spans types. peatProfile via the generic bourbon/rye-category fact.
